solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shampoo pup — it could become a new animal!

indicators.note: the clue says these letters could turn into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puppy fresh from its shampoo might be transformed into a whole new creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could become a new' tells you to rearrange SHAMPOO, PUP and IT; 'it' is part of the fodder, not just a filler word.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippo is a large African mammal, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Beneficiary's home — leading character seizing it meeting resistance

definitions.note: read as 'Beneficiary is', so the definition is the noun beneficiary, with the 's acting as the link

parts.note: to be at home is to be in

indicators.note: one piece grabs another and holds it inside itself

parts.note: the hero is the leading character of a story
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A legal note about who gets the house, with a principal figure taking hold of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who inherits property under a will is a beneficiary of that estate.

clue.text: Holy, penning heartless tale, very sad

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: pious means devout or holy

indicators.note: with its heart removed only the outer letters of the word tale remain

explanation.surface: A devout writer composing a callous story that turns out terribly sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing but means enclosing; 'heartless' removes the middle letters of the story word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something piteous arouses pity because it is deeply sorrowful.

clue.text: Sign pastries include small currants initially

indicators.note: the pastries take the next letters inside them

parts.note: pies are baked pastries
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word currants is used

explanation.surface: A baker's sign announcing pastries with a few small currants in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' puts S and C inside PIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisces, the fish, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Henry beset by metallic sound: object

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded, so the first letter sits inside the sound word

parts.note: a ting is the light ringing sound of struck metal
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry surrounded by clanging, staring at some item.
explanation.definitionFit: Thing is the general word for any physical item or article, so it is a synonym of object.

clue.text: Silly face

definitions.meaning: a silly as a noun is a foolish, gullible person

explanation.surface: A daft facial expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Mug is British slang both for a gullible fool and for the face.

clue.text: Group we enter with courage and love

indicators.note: the word we goes into the group word

parts.note: a set is a group of things
taken as written
heart means bravery, as in 'take heart'

explanation.surface: A rallying call: a group of us go in boldly and with affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is a common term of endearment, just as a sweetheart is a beloved person.

clue.text: Little Women's popular song

definitions.note: used as a noun, 'a little' means a tiny amount

parts.note: W is a standard abbreviation for women, as on clothing labels
a hit is a song that sells well

explanation.surface: A popular tune from the novel Little Women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Women' looks like the book title, but 'Little' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest amount, as in 'not a whit', so it means a tiny bit.

clue.text: Coastal feature, unique, captivating husband

indicators.note: to captivate here is to capture, holding the next letter inside

parts.note: single means the only one, so unique
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogical tables

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind seaside spot that has charmed a married man.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is the loose pebbles covering many beaches, a feature of the shore.

clue.text: Large dress must be altered, no matter what

indicators.note: a dress being altered is changed in shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dressmaker insisting that a big gown be taken in whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Regardless as an adverb means anyway, whatever the circumstances.

clue.text: Nobleman with award that's associated with organ?

definitions.note: the organ is the ear, and this is a part attached to it

parts.note: an earl is a British peer
the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: A peer who has just received an honour, linked somehow to a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The organ suggests music, but it is the hearing organ; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy lower lobe hangs from the outer ear, so it belongs to that organ.

clue.text: Good compere to write your article?

definitions.note: names a person hired to write something under someone else's name

parts.note: a compere is the host of a show

explanation.surface: Is a capable presenter the right person to pen your piece?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes someone who writes for you; the question mark marks it as a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter produces articles or books published under another person's name.

clue.text: Describing multisided shape in lagoon, act strangely

indicators.note: acting strangely suggests odd behaviour, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An odd-shaped thing behaves weirdly in a lagoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Octagonal is the adjective for a figure with eight sides, a many-sided shape.

clue.text: Perhaps painter from Hobart is talented

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: A gifted painter who comes from the Tasmanian city of Hobart.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is one example of a creative practitioner, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Something cutting your thistles, having edges, first and foremost??

definitions.text: Something cutting your thistles, having edges, first and foremost??

indicators.note: taking first literally, only the leading letter of each of the preceding words is used

parts.words: Something cutting your thistles, having edges

explanation.surface: A garden tool with a blade that slices through thistles before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both describes the tool and supplies its letters, the heads of the six words.
explanation.definitionFit: A scythe is a long curved blade on a pole, used for mowing weeds and grass.

clue.text: Church, different, with a London team?

definitions.note: names one example of a football club in London, hence the question mark

parts.note: else means other or different, as in 'someone else'

explanation.surface: A church congregation that has changed and now supports a London side.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a Premier League football club based in west London.

clue.text: From fish, a stench — move fast!

indicators.note: the letters are drawn out of the following words, across the comma

explanation.surface: A rotten fish smell is so strong you need to get away quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To hasten is to hurry, so it means to go quickly.

clue.text: Kind of wheat container you heard brought in

indicators.note: the next letter is carried into the container word

parts.note: a drum is a cylindrical container for oil and the like

indicators.note: the word you is said out loud, which gives the single letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you

explanation.surface: A grain bin that you were told had been delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns YOU into U, which 'brought in' places after the D of DRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Durum is a hard wheat variety ground for pasta.

clue.text: Fellow on leave getting fruit

parts.note: a fellow is a man
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: A man on holiday comes back with some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' seems to mean 'away on leave', but in a down clue it simply puts the fellow above the leaving word.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a sweet tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: Rage about extremely volatile person seeking to retaliate

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the following letters

parts.note: rage is extreme anger

indicators.note: only the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word volatile are used

explanation.surface: Fury in a hot-headed person bent on getting even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes just the first and last letters of 'volatile'; 'about' wraps the rage word around them.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger is someone who takes revenge for a wrong.

clue.text: Old money at court vanished

parts.note: ex means former, so old as in 'old flame'
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: Antique coins in a courtroom have disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is extinct when it has died out and is gone for good.

clue.text: Sailor cheers run

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British ways of saying thanks
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A seaman says thanks and then dashes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar (from tarpaulin) is old slang for a seaman.

clue.text: Son, daughter, holding article that's found on beach

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a substance lying on the shore, standing for a noun

indicators.note: the two letters grip the article between them

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A boy and girl clutching some object they picked up at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts AN between S and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaches are commonly covered in fine grains of worn rock.

clue.text: Possible to get over male's burnout after treatment

indicators.note: something treated is processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's exhaustion can be overcome once he has had therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To surmount a difficulty is to overcome it, so this means capable of being overcome.
